Cerebrospinal fluid testing later confirmed HSE. Despite treatment with intravenous acyclovir, the patient developed worsening right hemispheric edema with progressive midline shift, requiring external ventricular drain placement followed by emergent right decompressive hemicraniectomy. She subsequently improved without persistent focal neurologic deficits and later underwent cranioplasty. Our case highlights the importance of early recognition with neuroimaging, close neurologic monitoring, repeat imaging, and timely neurosurgical intervention in severe herpes simplex encephalitis complicated by malignant cerebral edema.

title: Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion-induced Deficits in Fine Skilled Motor Movement and Its Recovery Following Combined Treatment with Sodium Valproate and CIMT.
abstract: Preclinical studies have shown that sodium valproic acid (VPA) has neuroprotective properties following ischaemic injury. However, its compatibility as an adjuvant therapy with physical rehabilitation in ischaemic stroke recovery, with underlying neurophysiological mechanisms, has not been explored yet. The present study has investigated the advantage of combination therapy over monotherapy in ameliorating ischaemic stroke-induced deficits in skilled fine motor movements with associated changes in local and interhemispheric neural connectivity. Cerebral ischaemic stroke was induced by 60 min of middle cerebral artery occlusion in adult male Sprague-Dawley rats. VPA (300 mg/kg, subcutaneously, twice daily) was administered within 3 h after reperfusion and continued for 7 days, followed by constraint-induced movement therapy (CIMT) for another week (6 h/day). The ischaemic stroke phenotype was assessed based on neurological deficits, gait, forelimb use, rotarod stay time, reach success and infarct volume. Functional recovery, with associated changes in neural activities, was carried out by analysing the local field potential signals from the first reach success during the reach-to-grasp task on day 8 and day 15 post-stroke. Cortical oscillations were analysed at delta (0-4 Hz), theta (4-8 and 8-12 Hz) and beta (12-20 Hz) during the first reach success. Combination therapy after ischaemic stroke significantly improved motor and neurological functions compared to monotherapy and vehicle controls. The neural oscillations revealed a significant increase in theta power in the injured motor cortex after combination therapy when compared to that with monotherapy and control groups. The significant increase in the cross-correlation between hemispheres in the combination therapy group over monotherapy indicating an increased synchronised functional connectivity between the injured (left) and uninjured motor (right) cortices. Interestingly, VPA as monotherapy did not significantly reduce infarct volume compared to the vehicle controls. Furthermore, the therapeutic efficacy of monotherapies with VPA and early-onset CIMT (initiated immediately post-stroke) showed limited efficacy in promoting motor and neurological recovery. In conclusion, the study demonstrates that VPA combined with physical rehabilitative training (CIMT) enhances functional recovery by enhancing inter-hemispheric functional connectivity and represents a promising therapeutic strategy to alleviate persistent post-stroke motor deficits.

title: An exploratory simulation of the optimization of leukocyte transmigration, indicating that barrier routing is governed by context-dependent biochemical cues rather than hardwired programs.
abstract: Leukocyte infiltration across the blood-brain barrier contributes to many neuroinflammatory disorders, yet the physical mechanisms that determine how immune cells cross the barrier remain incompletely understood. In particular, it is unclear how leukocytes choose between paracellular migration through endothelial junctions and transcellular migration through the endothelial cell body. This question is especially relevant during central nervous system inflammation, where different T-lymphocyte subsets, including Th1 and Th17 cells, appear to preferentially use distinct migration routes. Previous studies have examined individual mechanical forces or upstream biochemical signaling pathways, but these approaches have not provided a unified framework that considers the energetic contributions of both the leukocyte and the deforming endothelium. To address this, we developed a two-route energy minimization model that incorporates an anisotropic, fiber-reinforced hyperelastic model, junctional unzipping, Helfrich membrane bending, caveolar vesicle fusion, and cytokine-dependent signaling. Model parameters were optimized, and route switching was evaluated using Sobol global sensitivity analysis to determine which specific mechanical and signaling parameters independently drive route switching rather than merely scaling overall energy magnitude. The model reproduced the experimental validation conditions used in this study and identified distinct regimes of mechanical control. Under IFN-γ-dominant conditions, route selection was influenced primarily by ICAM-1 adhesion kinetics. Under IL-17-dominant conditions, control shifted toward PECAM-1-related physical properties and their nonlinear interactions, which accounted for 76% of the variance in route switching. These exploratory findings suggest that leukocyte transmigration is shaped by local biochemical conditions together with the mechanical properties of the endothelial barrier, rather than by a single fixed migration program. Mapping the associated energetic landscape may help clarify the physical factors governing immune-cell entry into the central nervous system and provide a framework for studying mechanisms that regulate leukocyte trafficking during neuroinflammation.

title: Tensor decomposition reveals discrete cortical reorganization under graded propofol anesthesia.
abstract: Although propofol-induced anesthesia is known to suppress consciousness by promoting low-frequency frontal oscillations through thalamocortical circuits, a comprehensive understanding of its whole-brain coupling feature set remains elusive. Specifically, the global reorganization of nonlinear cross-frequency coupling remains poorly characterized due to analytical limitations. We analyzed 64-channel EEG data from 17 participants across five states (awake and target propofol concentrations of 1, 2, 3, and 4 mcg/ml, defined as States 1 to 5). After computing time-frequency representation (TFR) and bicoherence, Parallel Factor Analysis (PARAFAC) was used to extract unbiased spatio-spectral components from both linear and nonlinear measures. PARAFAC decomposition isolated distinct linear and nonlinear neurodynamic components driving the anesthetic transition. While linear spectral features and signal complexity transitioned in a gradual, monotonic manner. PARAFAC tensor decomposition of high-dimensional whole-brain bicoherence identified two robust, intrinsically decoupled nonlinear components with distinct spatial-spectral profiles. Model comparison demonstrated that frontal slow-wave self-coupling (Component 1) undergoes a discrete, stepwise state-space reconfiguration during loss of consciousness, whereas posterior alpha coupling (Component 2) exhibits a smooth, continuous decay with propofol titration. Phase-space kinetic trajectories confirmed a highly directed transition at unconsciousness onset, followed by confined local oscillations during deep anesthesia. This multi-dimensional decomposition framework captures discrete versus continuous neural dynamics, providing objective, state-sensitive biomarkers for precisely monitoring anesthesia depth and cortical state transitions.

title: Basal Forebrain Volume is Associated With Cortical Amyloid Burden in Cognitively Unimpaired Older Adults at Varying Genetic Risk for Alzheimer's Disease.
journal: The American journal of geriatric psychiatry. Open science, education, and practice
abstract: In mild cognitive impairment and dementia due to Alzheimer's disease (AD), postmortem and in vivo neuroimaging studies have demonstrated significant neuronal loss in the basal forebrain cholinergic system (BFCS), which provides the primary cholinergic input to the cerebral cortex. Within the BFCS, atrophy is most prominent in the nucleus basalis of Meynert (nbM), a posteriorly located cluster of magnocellular neurons. However, less is known surrounding the relationship between amyloid deposition, BFCS atrophy, and medial temporal lobe (MTL) volume loss in preclinical AD. This study investigates the relationship between BFCS sub-regional volume and Aβ burden in cognitively unimpaired middle-aged individuals. Cognitively unimpaired participants aged 50-67 with a first-degree family history for AD were genetically screened to three groups matched for age and sex: APOE genotype ε4ε4, ε3ε4, and ε3ε3 (n = 15 each). Aβ burden was calculated using distribution volumes ratios (DVR) using [11C]PiB-PET, with a whole cerebellum reference region. BFCS and MTL subregional volumes (i.e., entorhinal cortex, hippocampus, amygdala, parahippocampal gyrus) were extracted using 3T-MRI. nbM, but not other BFCS regions, was found to be inversely associated with global Aβ burden (Pearson r(43) = -0.40, p = 0.004). When stratified by Aβ-positivity, the observed inverse association was limited to Aβ+ participants (Pearson r(9) = -0.7, p = 0.008). MTL volumes were not consistently associated with global Aβ burden. We observed nbM, but not MTL volume, to show robust inverse association with cortical amyloid burden in cognitively unimpaired, Aβ+, middle-aged adults. These findings provide further in vivo evidence suggesting that nbM atrophy is an early structural correlate of AD pathogenesis, potentially preceding MTL atrophy.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists in Alzheimer's disease and MCI: a meta-analysis.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia in older individuals and remains a major clinical and socioeconomic burden. Despite the success of anti-amyloid therapies in reducing biomarker burden, more effective and safer treatments are still needed. Given the emerging evidence of a role for metabolic dysfunction and brain insulin resistance in AD pathophysiology, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have been proposed as potential disease-modifying therapies. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to April 22, 2026 to evaluate the efficacy and safety of GLP-1 RAs in AD and mild cognitive impairment. Randomized controlled trials comparing GLP-1 RAs with placebo, standard care, or non-intervention across the Alzheimer's continuum were eligible; abstracts and studies with unavailable results were excluded. Random-effects models were used. Risk ratios (RRs) were calculated for binary outcomes, and mean or standardized mean differences for continuous outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Seven studies comprising 4132 participants met the inclusion criteria. The mean age of the pooled studies was 72.1 years, while the mean baseline Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) varied from 2.71 to 3.8. GLP-1 RAs were not associated with significant improvement in cognition (Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale: standard mean difference -0.05; 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.12 to 0.02; p = 0.1928) or disease progression (CDR-SB: mean difference: 0.09; 95% CI: -0.10 to 0.28; p = 0.362). They were associated with a higher frequency of adverse events (RR 1.07; 95% CI: 1.04 to 1.10; p < 0.0001) and weight loss (RR 5.01; 95% CI: 3.99 to 6.27; p < 0.0001). Biomarker and neuroimaging findings were inconsistent and failed to translate to clinical benefit. GLP-1 RAs did not improve cognitive or functional outcomes in AD and were associated with adverse events. Their role may be better explored in biomarker-enriched, metabolically selected populations or assessment of GLP-1 RAs with greater brain penetrance.

title: Orbital metastasis revealing occult metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma in a South African man: A rare initial ophthalmic presentation.
abstract: Orbital metastasis is a rare initial presentation of undiagnosed prostate cancer. We report a 65-year-old South African man presenting with a one-year history of progressive, painless right upper eyelid swelling, proptosis, tearing, and vision loss. Imaging revealed a right lateral orbital mass causing bone erosion. An incisional biopsy confirmed metastatic adenocarcinoma with strong prostate-specific antigen positivity. Further evaluation showed an irregular prostate, a serum PSA of 1620 ng/mL, urinary retention, nodal involvement, and extensive bone metastases. A prostate biopsy confirmed high-grade disease (Gleason 9). This case underscores considering a prostatic primary in older men with suspicious orbital masses.

title: Normative data of laser evoked potentials using Nd:YAP laser.
abstract: To establish a robust multi-centre normative database for Nd:YAP laser-evoked potentials (LEPs) across distal and proximal stimulation sites, and to quantify the impact of laser spot size (energy density) and demographic factors on LEP parameters. One hundred nine healthy adults (57 females) were recruited from three centres (Geneva, Lyon, Saint-Etienne). Nd:YAP laser pulses were delivered with a 3-mm beam (Centre 1) or 4-mm beam (Centres 2-3). LEPs were recorded from standard EEG sites (including Fz/Cz/Pz and contralateral temporal leads). Stimulation sites included hand dorsum (n = 109), foot dorsum (n = 80), thigh and upper neck (both n = 43). N1, N2, and P2 latencies and amplitudes were measured and normal limits estimated as mean ± 99.9% confidence interval. ANCOVA (age-corrected) tested spot-size effects; repeated-measures ANOVA tested site effects; correlations assessed age/height associations. The vertex N2-P2 complex was consistently recorded across centres and sites (100% for hand, thigh, neck; ∼97% for foot). N1 detection was less consistent, particularly with larger spot size and at the foot. Smaller spot size (higher energy density) yielded shorter N2/P2 latencies and larger N2-P2 amplitudes for hand stimulation, and shorter P2 latency for foot stimulation. Sex and height showed no significant effects. Increasing age was associated with longer N2/P2 latencies and reduced N2-P2 amplitudes for distal sites, with minimal age effects at proximal sites. This study provides the most comprehensive Nd:YAP LEP normative dataset to date, including distal and proximal sites and spot-size-specific reference limits. These data support standardized, high-specificity clinical interpretation of LEPs for assessing small-fibre and spinothalamic pathway dysfunction.

title: Selective mGlu1 Receptor Activation Restores Cortical Inhibitory Tone and Improves Cognitive Performance in a Subchronic Phencyclidine NMDA Hypofunction Model.
abstract: Deficits in prefrontal cortex (PFC) inhibitory transmission are thought to underlie the cognitive symptoms of schizophrenia that remain untreated by current pharmacotherapies. The metabotropic glutamate 1 (mGlu1) receptor, a subtype of the mGlu receptor family, is a promising therapeutic target because its activation enhances inhibitory transmission in the PFC through the excitation of somatostatin-expressing GABAergic (gamma-aminobutyric acidergic) interneurons (SST-INs). We used a subchronic phencyclidine (PCP) NMDA receptor antagonist mouse model, mGlu1 positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), and mice with selective deletion of mGlu1 receptors from SST-INs to examine the cell type-specific role of mGlu1 signaling in cortical inhibition and cognition. We used ex vivo whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology to assess inhibitory transmission in the PFC, and cognitive performance was evaluated using tests of working memory and novel object recognition. Subchronic PCP treatment impaired inhibitory synaptic transmission in the PFC, particularly onto layer V pyramidal neurons projecting to the nucleus accumbens. Pharmacological activation of mGlu1 restored inhibitory drive and reversed PCP-induced deficits in working memory and novel object recognition. Importantly, selective deletion of mGlu1 receptors from SST-INs abolished the ability of mGlu1 activation to restore cortical inhibition and cognitive function, demonstrating that these receptors are required for the therapeutic effects of mGlu1 PAMs. These findings identify SST-IN-expressed mGlu1 receptors as critical regulators of prefrontal cortical inhibition and cognition. Positive allosteric modulation of mGlu1 represents a promising therapeutic strategy for treating cognitive deficits associated with schizophrenia by restoring inhibitory circuit function.

title: Intratumoral and Peritumoral Functional Connectivity Reveals Network-Level Signatures of Glioma.
abstract: Gliomas are recognized as network-level diseases that remodel functional connectivity across the brain. Using resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) data from 306 patients with pathologically confirmed glioma at two hospitals, we delineated individualized intra- and peritumoral functional networks to quantify tumor-related alterations. Two novel indices-the ratio of intratumoral functional regions (RIFR) and ratio of peritumoral tumor-related regions (RPTR)-were proposed to describe network remodeling. Both indices were related to pathological, structural, functional, cognitive, language, and survival measures. Lower RIFR indicated diminished intratumoral connectivity and worse prognosis, while higher values reflected preserved network integration and longer survival. Models incorporating network features yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.90 in training and 0.86-0.88 in external validation. Supporting analyses suggested that intratumoral functional regions are associated with distinct molecular and cellular characteristics. These findings suggest that intra- and peritumoral networks reflect biologically and functionally distinct tumor subregions and are associated with network-level alterations, brain function, and patient outcome. Interpretation is limited by the hemodynamic basis of rs-fMRI, incomplete data, and limited intraoperative validation. These findings identify individualized intra- and peritumoral connectivity measures as candidate markers of glioma-associated network remodeling and prognosis that require prospective, multimodal validation.

title: Insights Into RP2-Associated Retinopathy: From Molecular Basis to Clinical Translation.
abstract: Pathogenic variants in RP2 cause X-linked RP2-associated retinopathy, a rare inherited retinal disorder typically characterized by childhood onset and progression to severe visual impairment within the first three decades of life. Despite its clinical severity, comprehensive clinical and genetic data on RP2-associated retinopathy remain limited and no therapeutic approaches have yet progressed toward clinical application. Here, we provide an overview of current molecular, clinical, and therapeutic knowledge on RP2-associated retinopathy together with an analysis of the spectrum and distribution of clinically classified, ClinVar-curated variants. Analysis of 325 ACMG/AMP Class 3-5 variants revealed that among pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants, frameshift and nonsense variants predominated, supporting loss of RP2 function as the major disease mechanism as previously described. In contrast, variants of uncertain significance were largely missense variants, underscoring the particular challenge of missense variant interpretation in RP2. Exon distribution of RP2 variants did not deviate from expectation for Class 3 variants, or for Class 4 and 5 variants in exons 2-4. However, we observed a significant enrichment of Class 4/5 variants in exon 1, driven mainly by initiator codon variants, and a depletion of Class 4/5 variants in exon 5. By integrating published knowledge on molecular mechanisms, genetic variants, clinical progression, and therapeutic development, with a detailed analysis of ClinVar-annotated RP2 variants, this narrative review outlines the current understanding of RP2-associated retinopathy and identifies key gaps that will need to be addressed for therapeutic development and clinical translation. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06982417.

title: Pathways to Binge Eating Among Black Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Grounded Theory Qualitative Study.
abstract: Black adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) are at higher risk for binge eating and often face challenges in achieving blood glucose control, which may be due to untreated disordered eating. Little is known about the influences on their eating behaviors in the context of T2D. This study explores factors influencing binge eating in Black adults with T2D and the perspectives of the diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) providers treating them. Black adults with T2D experiencing at least two self-reported binge eating episodes a month (n = 14) and DSMES providers (n = 8) who treated this population participated in in-depth interviews. Interviews explored experiences with managing T2D and facilitators of binge eating. A constructivist grounded theory approach was used to analyze the data and develop a framework explaining factors influencing binge eating in this population. Participants identified multilevel stressors and barriers that influenced their binge eating episodes and treatment. These factors ranged from societal to individual-level and physiological factors that led to active food restriction, emotional eating, feelings of deprivation, and binge eating. Providers acknowledged limited training in disordered eating and weight stigma and identified gaps in current DSMES. Binge eating in Black adults with T2D is shaped by structural, cultural, and psychological factors. Incorporating culturally responsive guidance, emotion-focused coping strategies, and routine screening for disordered eating into diabetes care may improve engagement and glycemic outcomes for this population.

title: Blood-brain barrier junctional proteins as potential biomarkers of cerebral ischaemia and reperfusion injury.
abstract: Cerebral ischaemia/reperfusion (CI/R) damage involves obstructing the blood supply to the brain, followed by restoring cerebral circulation through thrombolytic treatment. The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a specialised structure separating the brain from peripheral blood circulation and plays an important role in brain function. However, little is known about CI/R-induced BBB damage and changes in circulatory biomarkers. This novel study aims to examine the changes in BBB tight-junctional (TJ) proteins (Zonula occludens-1, Occludin and Claudin-5) in the hippocampus of the brain and determine the levels of these proteins in a mouse model of CI/R induced by bilateral common carotid occlusion. Expressions of BBB TJ proteins in the hippocampus were examined by immunohistochemistry and Western blotting. The levels of these proteins in blood serum were measured by Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay. The results showed a significant decrease in BBB TJ proteins in the hippocampus, with increased levels of these proteins in blood serum in ischaemic mice as compared to sham-operated mice suggesting that these proteins can be used as potential biomarkers for the diagnosis of CI/R injury.

title: A cross-sectional study of the prevalence and correlates of post-traumatic stress among people attending acceptance and commitment therapy for chronic pain.
abstract: Experiences of trauma are common among people with chronic pain, although estimates of comorbid post-traumatic stress vary widely across contexts. Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), which targets psychological flexibility to improve pain-related functioning, is increasingly delivered for people with pain. To inform treatment delivery, understanding of the prevalence and correlates of post-traumatic stress among those attending ACT-based treatment for pain is needed. This study aimed to identify the prevalence of post-traumatic stress and its associations with key pain-related outcomes and other relevant psychosocial factors at the start of an ACT-based treatment. This was a cross-sectional study using data collected within routine clinical care at a speciality pain management service in the UK. Four hundred and fifty-one participants completed standardized self-report questionnaires of post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS), pain-related outcomes (pain intensity and interference, work and social adjustment, and depression symptoms), psychological flexibility/inflexibility, and stigma at the start of an interdisciplinary ACT-based treatment for chronic pain. Forty-seven percent of patients (n = 213) reported a traumatic exposure and 30% of the sample reported clinically meaningful PTSS. Greater severity of PTSS and probable post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) were associated with significantly worse pain-related outcomes, psychological flexibility/inflexibility, and stigma in bivariate analyses. PTSS severity and probable PTSD showed significant unique associations with poorer pain outcomes in regression models controlling for covariates and psychological flexibility/inflexibility. Post-traumatic stress is common among people engaging in ACT-based treatment for pain and associated with adverse pain outcomes. Trauma-informed practice is therefore important when providing ACT-based treatment for pain.

title: Convergent and Distinct Transcriptional Signatures in Suicide, Bipolar Disorder, and Major Depressive Disorder.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Globally, a person dies by suicide every 40 seconds, underscoring a major global public health concern. In the United States, suicide is the second leading cause of death among individuals aged 10-34 years. Suicide is a complex, multifactorial phenomenon influenced by genetic and epigenetic factors and is strongly associated with mood disorders, particularly major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder (BD). However, the extent to which their molecular signatures converge or diverge across disorders and brain regions remains incompletely understood. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic literature review of suicide, MDD, and BD transcriptomic studies in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science. Eligible studies used human postmortem brain tissue, reported a complete genome-wide transcriptomic list of differentially expressed genes (DEG), and compared suicide decedents with psychiatric non-suicide individuals diagnosed with the same underlying disorder. Regarding BD, studies comparing affected individuals to unaffected controls were included. Single-cell and peripheral-blood studies were excluded because unavailable for suicide. Curated suicide and BD DEG datasets were integrated with a published bulk transcriptomic dataset of MDD. We identified both shared and disease-specific molecular signatures across suicide, BD, and MDD, and identified DEGs shared across brain regions and those that were region-specific. A total of 276 genes were shared across all three conditions, implicating cellular stress, hypoxia (VEGFA, ADM, NDRG1, DDIT4), immune and inflammatory signaling through TNFα/NF-κB (IL1B, ICAM1, NFE2L2) and IL6-JAK-STAT3 pathways (STAT3, SOCS3, IL1R1m OSMR), complement activation (CIR, SERPiNA1, LGALS3), extracellular matrix remodeling (COL4A1, SERPINH1, PLOD2), and unfolded protein response (BAG3, WFS1, MTHFD2). Suicide-associated DEGs were prominently downregulated, and involved metal-ion homeostasis, stress responses, synaptic regulation, and circadian pathways, whereas BD showed downregulation in synaptic and vesicle-related processes alongside region-specific metabolic dysregulation. MDD exhibited changes in RNA processing, ribosomal function, and protein synthesis. Genetic integration revealed that 133 genes shared between BD and MDD had gene variants associated with the corresponding condition per GWAS. Transcription factor analysis identified 20 regulatory factors with altered activity across all three conditions despite differences in their predicted downstream targets. Overall, these findings suggest that suicide, MDD, and BD share aspects of their molecular and regulatory pathophysiology while exhibiting distinct patterns, including in a region-specific manner.

title: Isl1 + Central Amygdala Neurons Coordinate Control of the Jaw and Stomach During Ingestion.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Central Amygdala neurons expressing Isl1 (CeA Isl1+ ) project to brainstem regions involved in control of the jaw and the stomach, including the parabrachial nucleus (PBN), the nucleus of the tractus solitary (NTS), and the parvocellular reticular nucleus (PCRt). Stimulation of CeA Isl1+ cells elicits fictive feeding, particularly biting. Activation of these neurons can rate dependently set the amplitude of bite force and inhibition dramatically reduces bite force. Findings suggest this force generation depends on modulation of a jaw closing reflex involving tooth sensory neurons in the mesencephalic trigeminal nucleus (Me5). Anatomical tracing studies show Me5 neurons receive synaptic input from CeA Isl1+ neurons. Patch clamp recordings of Me5 neurons indicate this synapse is mediated by GABA yet depolarizing. Activation of CeA Isl1+ neurons is capable of dramatically potentiating the periodontal jaw closing reflex, a reflex whereby Me5 tooth sensory neurons activate jaw closing muscles. In addition to controlling the actions of the jaw, CeA Isl1+ neuron stimulation is sufficient to reduce gastric pH. Inhibition experiments show these cells are necessary for lowering gastric pH in mice anticipating a meal. Finally, CeA Isl1+ neurons can modulate gastric motility, stimulation transiently suppresses gastric motility, an effect also observed when animals chewed food. Subdiaphragmatic vagotomy eliminated the transient suppression of gastric motility otherwise observed with CeA Isl1+ neuron stimulation or food chewing. Taken together, this molecularly and anatomically defined population generates specific motor patterns of ingestion that involve not only release of oromotor patterns, but also modulation of gastric functions.

title: Detection of the RNA-Editing Enzyme ADARB1 in Primary Auditory Neurons and Anti-ADARB1 Immunofluorescence as a Means for Automated Counting.
journal: The journal of histochemistry and cytochemistry : official journal of the Histochemistry Society
abstract: Spiral ganglion neurons (SGNs), the primary auditory afferents in the inner ear, are vulnerable to degeneration from neuropathies, concussion, and aging, among other causes. Accurate quantification of SGNs is critical for assessing degeneration and therapeutic interventions, but manual counting is arduous due to dense cellular crowding and unreliable nuclear markers. Because SGNs receive input from GluA2-containing AMPA receptors, the transcripts for which must be RNA-edited for calcium impermeability, we hypothesized that SGNs express high levels of the RNA-editing enzyme ADARB1. Here, we confirm enriched expression of Adarb1 transcripts in SGNs and show that anti-ADARB1 antibodies robustly label the nuclei of type I and type II SGNs from young and aged mice, adult macaques, and adult humans. Neuronal versus glial specificity was confirmed using antibodies against neurofilament heavy chain (NFH), human antigen D (HuD), GATA binding protein 3 (GATA3), and SRY-box 2 (SOX2). A blinded investigator manually counted mouse SGNs via NFH, and these were compared to automated counts of ADARB1-positive nuclei using the analyze particles function in ImageJ. A concordance correlation coefficient and Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated strong agreement between the manual and automated counts. Together, these results suggest broad utility of ADARB1 immunolabeling for automated counts of SGNs across species.

title: Channelrhodopsin ion selectivity determines mechanisms and efficacy of optogenetic defibrillation in human atria and ventricles.
abstract: Cardiac re-entrant arrhythmias are a major cause of sudden cardiac death. Optogenetic defibrillation has emerged as a promising anti-arrhythmic strategy based on photoactivation of channelrhodopsins, yet the efficacy and potential adverse consequences of activating different classes of light-gated ion channels have not been systematically evaluated. Previous studies assessed either cation (e.g. ChR2) or anion (e.g. GtACR1) non-selective channels, both of which depolarize resting cardiomyocytes. Recently identified light-gated K+ channels (e.g. WiChR) suppress cardiomyocyte activity while maintaining the membrane potential near its resting state, but their defibrillation potential remains unexplored. We used computational simulations to compare ChR2, GtACR1 and WiChR. Single-cell simulations showed that ChR2 and GtACR1 markedly increased diastolic intracellular Ca2+ (by 42.6% and 52.6%, respectively), whereas WiChR induced only minimal changes (by 4.0%), suggesting lower pro-arrhythmogenic risk. WiChR, however, slightly increased intracellular Na+ (by 15.1% vs. 0.1% and 3.4% for ChR2 and GtACR1), consistent with the residual Na+ permeability of currently available K+-conducting channelrhodopsins. Simulations in human ventricles and atria showed that GtACR1 most effectively terminated re-entrant arrhythmias at low light intensities, whereas WiChR achieved comparable efficacy at ≥5 mW/mm2. Complementary tissue-scale simulations revealed that defibrillation occurs through depolarization within the excitable gap followed by fast Na+ channel inactivation (ChR2 and partly GtACR1), or through reduced membrane resistance at sufficiently high light intensities (large-conductance channels GtACR1 and WiChR). Overall, we demonstrate that channelrhodopsin ion selectivity is a key determinant of both optogenetic defibrillation efficacy and its underlying mechanisms. TRANSLATIONAL PERSPECTIVE: Re-entrant arrhythmias are a leading cause of sudden cardiac death. Standard therapies, including the activation of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, carry burdens such as pain and myocardial injury. Optogenetic defibrillation has been suggested as a potentially gentler alternative, replacing high-voltage electrical shocks by photoactivation of light-gated ion channels expressed in cardiac cells. Determining which light-gated ion channel optimally balances efficacy and adverse effects on cardiac electrophysiology is critical for clinical translation. We addressed this question using computational simulations and validation experiments in zebrafish hearts. We identify ion selectivity as a key determinant of both the success rate for arrhythmia termination and the underlying mechanisms: non-selective cation- and anion-conducting channels terminate re-entry efficiently while promoting intracellular Ca2+ accumulation, a plausible substrate for pro-arrhythmic side effects that could undermine therapeutic safety. K+-conducting channels largely avoid this pro-arrhythmic risk by holding cardiomyocytes near their resting potential, albeit at the cost of requiring transmural illumination, while also causing mild Na+ accumulation attributable to residual Na+ permeability. Together, these trade-offs define clear clinical implications: K+-conducting channels may provide the safest option for optogenetic defibrillation, particularly once variants with further enhanced K+ selectivity and red-shifted activation spectra for improved operation within blood-perfused myocardium become available. KEY POINTS: We use computational simulations to compare cation non-selective (ChR2), anion non-selective (GtACR1) and K+-selective (WiChR) channelrhodopsins for optogenetic termination of re-entrant arrhythmia. Single-cardiomyocyte simulations suggest that ChR2 and GtACR1 activation can cause progressive accumulation of intracellular Ca2+, which is minimized when using WiChR. Intracellular microelectrode recordings from hearts of transgenic adult zebrafish validate the simulated voltage dynamics seen with ChR2, GtACR1 or WiChR activation. Simulations of human left ventricles and atria indicate that GtACR1 is most effective in terminating re-entrant arrhythmia at low light intensities, whereas WiChR becomes similarly effective at higher intensities. Tissue-scale simulations indicate distinct defibrillation mechanisms: excitable gap extinction by de novo action potential initiation followed by inactivation of fast Na+ channels for depolarizing channelrhodopsins (ChR2, GtACR1), and reduction in membrane resistance for the large-conductance channels (GtACR1, WiChR), effectively clamping the membrane potential at each channel's reversal potential at high light levels.

title: Accelerated Motion-Compensated Diffusion-Weighted pCASL Using Subspace Low-Rank Reconstruction for Quantification of BBB Water Exchange and Permeability.
abstract: To develop an accelerated motion-compensated diffusion-weighted pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (MCDW-pCASL) method using a spatial subspace low-rank reconstruction method for efficient quantification of blood-brain barrier (BBB) water exchange (kw) and permeability (PSw). An accelerated multidelay MCDW-pCASL sequence was developed to simultaneously encode intravascular and extravascular diffusion-weighted ASL signals across multiple post-labeling delays (PLDs). A spatial subspace low-rank reconstruction framework was optimized to enable joint estimation of cerebral blood flow (CBF) and BBB water exchange rate and permeability. Fourteen young healthy adults underwent test-retest scans (separated by ∼1 week) at 3 T with both the accelerated MCDW-pCASL (acceleration factor = 3) and a conventional diffusion-prepared (DP) pCASL sequence. Whole-brain, gray-matter, and white-matter CBF and kw values were quantified to assess test-retest repeatability and cross-method agreement. An additional cohort of 30 older adults underwent single-session MCDW and DP scans to evaluate age-related perfusion and BBB kw/PSw differences. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) were used to assess reliability and agreement. Accelerated MCDW-pCASL demonstrated excellent agreement with DP-pCASL for CBF (ICC = 0.89) and fair agreement for kw (ICC = 0.56). Test-retest repeatability of MCDW-pCASL was good for CBF, BBB, kw, and PSw (ICC ≈ 0.6). Across both sequences, younger subjects exhibited significantly higher CBF and kw compared with older adults. Incorporating a spatial low-rank subspace reconstruction enables accelerated MCDW-pCASL acquisition with reliable simultaneous quantification of CBF, BBB kw, and PSw. Clinical applications of this method for assessing perfusion and BBB function are warranted.

title: The effect of resveratrol on the hippocampus in the pentylenetetrazol (PTZ) - dependent kindling model of epilepsy.
abstract: Epilepsy is a long-term neurological condition marked by neuronal excitotoxicity, oxidative stress, and inflammation of the nervous system. This study seeks to explore the neuroprotective and anti-seizure properties of Resveratrol (RSV) and the molecular processes involved in a pentylenetetrazol (PTZ)-induced kindling epilepsy model, with a focus on ion channels, apoptosis, and SIRT1 pathway. A total of thirty-two Wistar albino rats were assigned into four groups: Sham, RSV, PTZ, and PTZ + RSV. Following kindling induction via PTZ (35 mg/kg, 3 days/week) or equivalent saline administration for control groups, subsequent RSV treatment (5 mg/kg/day, i.p.) or saline was administered for 28 days. Brain tissues were harvested 24 h after the final injection. Epileptic activity was captured through the use of electrocorticography (ECoG), while tissue damage to the hippocampus was evaluated via hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining. Molecular levels of SIRT1, Caspase-3, and S100B protein were assessed via immunofluorescence, whereas SERCA2a, CACNA1G, HCN2, Caspase-3, Caspase-9, and SIRT1 gene expression levels were measured through qPCR analysis. RSV treatment greatly extended the initial myoclonic jerk delay (p = 0.0001) and lowered both the seizure phase and total spike count compared to the PTZ group. Microscopic examination revealed that RSV maintained tissue health by reducing neuronal deterioration and inflammation in the hippocampal CA1 area. Immunofluorescence analysis revealed that RSV treatment restored SIRT1 levels, which were previously diminished by PTZ, and significantly reduced the elevated markers of apoptosis and glial activation. Furthermore, qPCR analysis demonstrated that RSV treatment significantly reversed PTZ-induced gene expression alterations by upregulating the expressions of SERCA2α, CACNA1G, HCN2, and SIRT1 (p < 0.0001), while downregulating the expressions of Caspase-3 and Caspase-9. RSV exerts significant neuroprotective effects in the PTZ kindling model by modulating the SIRT1-mediated stress response and preventing neuronal apoptosis. Notably, this study provides the first in vivo evidence that RSV modulates SERCA2a, CACNA1G, and HCN2 ion channel gene expressions to control intracellular calcium balance and neuronal excitability during epileptogenesis.

title: A microglial basis for fragile X syndrome via impairment of FMRP-regulated lysosomal function.
abstract: Silencing of the FMRP-encoding FMR1 gene results in fragile X syndrome (FXS), the most common inheritable intellectual disability and autism. FMRP regulates various neuronal functions but clinical trials targeting neurons have failed, suggesting unrecognized disease mechanisms. We find that mice with selective Fmr1 deletion in microglia exhibit audiogenic seizures (AGS) and parvalbumin (PV) neuron loss, recapitulating two key phenotypes observed in FXS (Fmr1-/y) mice. By combining snRNA-Seq and RNA immunoprecipitation, we identify several lysosomal mRNAs as FMRP binding targets. FMRP promotes lysosomal protein expression and its deficiency disrupts lysosomal function in microglia. Notably, FMRP depletion reduces Grn-encoded secretory progranulin and increases PV neuron apoptosis in immature brains. PV neuron density is decreased similarly in Grn+/-, Fmr1-/y, and Grn+/-;Fmr1-/y mice, and progranulin overexpression rescues AGS and PV neuron loss in Fmr1-/y mice. Thus, our study identifies microglia and progranulin as critical regulators of FXS pathogenesis and potential targets for FXS therapy.

title: Brain imaging in dystrophinopathies.
abstract: Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophies (DMD, BMD) are caused by genetic variants in the DMD gene coding dystrophin proteins. In addition to the impairment of muscular function, these patients also present frequent cognitive and neuropsychiatric disorders due to impaired expression of several brain dystrophins: Dp427, Dp140 and Dp71. Cerebral imaging has shed new light on the impact of dystrophinopathies on brain structure, function, and connectivity. We review the brain imaging results obtained in patients and divers animal models, showing presence of mild cortical atrophy, slight modifications of structures volumes, decreased cerebral blood flood, white matter microstructure alterations, brain hypometabolism, altered connectivity, and an abnormal cerebral response to stress. We further discuss the putative progression of cerebral disorders, and their variable severity when Dp140 expression is affected in addition to that of Dp427. Some correlations between imaging parameters and cognitive and psychological impairments have been reported but remain to be confirmed.

title: CD4+ T Cell Activation and Peripheral Immune Cell Influx into the Brain Following Wildfire Smoke Exposure is Modulated by a Saturated Fat Diet.
abstract: Over the past 40 years, wildfires across the United States have steadily increased, in terms of acreage burned. Smoke from wildfires can exacerbate several cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, with new studies highlighting potential sustained neurological outcomes. The purpose of this study was to delineate the role of peripheral immune populations in woodsmoke-induced neuroinflammation, the timeline of this response, and the impact of diet on each of these factors. Based on previous research on other pollutants and diet introduction, we included a highly saturated fatty acid (coconut oil) to represent the effects of a diet intervention that may modulate the severity and time course of peripheral immune infiltration. 8-week-old female C57BL/6 mice were exposed to either a sham filtered air or a woodsmoke exposure of a 0.5mg/m3 concentration every other day for 14 days, 4hr/day. Three time points were analyzed: 1-, 14-, and 28-days post exposure to woodsmoke to determine neuroinflammation at its peak and when it begins to resolve. At each time point, brains were queried by high dimensional flow cytometry analysis. Markers for peripheral immune infiltration included T cells (CD3, CD4), lymphocyte trafficking (LFA-1), resident immune cells (CD11b, ACSA-2) and other inflammation-dependent markers. Endothelial cell populations (CD31) and relevant adhesion molecules (VCAM-1, ICAM-1) were also analyzed. Results demonstrate a time and diet-dependent influx of CD4 T cells (Cd11b-, CD3+, CD4+, RORγ-, FOXP3-, CD44+), potentially to resolve neuroinflammation from woodsmoke inhalation. We also see a pattern of inflammation across several trafficking and adhesion markers, including LFA-1, VCAM-1 and ICAM-1, that peaks at 1 day after the last exposure (14 days after the initial insult). Conferred with these results are metabolomic changes in the brain including upregulated taurine and glycerolipid metabolism that is mainly tied to increased susceptibility to inflammatory phenotypes in the brain. Here, we demonstrate that woodsmoke inhalation can initiate the recruitment of peripheral immune populations and activation of endothelial cell markers within the brain. The presence of these cells implicates a larger, more persistent impact on the central nervous system following woodsmoke exposure.

title: Ketamine administration reduced conditioned defensive behaviour and upregulated protein expression associated with neuroplasticity in a planarian model of aversive memory reactivation.
abstract: Traumatic memories that are resistant to modification or extinction are a characteristic feature of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The process of fear memory reconsolidation has been identified as a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of PTSD. Ketamine, an NMDA receptor antagonist with dissociative properties, has been identified as a drug with high therapeutic potential for this target, as it destabilises traumatic memory while enabling rapid modification and update of the memory to no longer be threatening. However, its exact mechanisms of action on reducing the impact of aversive memory remains poorly understood. To better understand these mechanisms, a conditioned aversive memory reactivation model using ketamine was carried out in brown planaria (Girardia dorotocephala), an invertebrate model that shows a high degree of conservation in neural anatomy, receptors, neurotransmitters, and learning behaviours, while being comparatively simpler than standard mammalian models. In this study, 15 planaria were randomly assigned to three treatment groups (10 μM ketamine, 1 μM ketamine, vehicle control) and underwent a classical aversive memory reactivation paradigm. Whole planaria were processed for an exploratory proteomic analysis to analyse changes in protein expression associated with the effects of ketamine on the aversive memory reactivation process. Behavioural data showed a significant reduction in defensive behaviours, including scrunching movements F(2,12) = 11.85, p = 0.0014, ƞ2 = 0.66, C-shape movements F(2,12) = 6.59, p = 0.012, ƞ2 = 0.52, and head turns F(2,12) = 9.59, p = 0.0032, ƞ2 = 0.61, in the 10 μM ketamine group on the final test day compared to vehicle controls. Proteomic analysis showed that these behavioural changes were accompanied by a high degree of enrichment in molecular pathways associated with rapid neuronal growth and synaptic plasticity, and changes in cellular mRNA, all markers of learning. These preliminary findings in an invertebrate model improve understanding of how ketamine may facilitate disruption of conditioned aversive memory via rapid neuronal restructuring and augmenting synaptic plasticity.

title: Precise modeling of task-related sensorimotor activation based on simultaneous surface electromyography.
abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the relationship between motor control of ankle movements and actual motor performance using simultaneous functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and surface electromyography (EMG) in healthy individuals. Twenty participants performed dorsi-/plantarflexion of the ankle (Ankle) and gait imagery in a block design during fMRI. First-level models consisting of task regressors included either orthogonalized accelerometry (Acc) from the foot, EMG from the tibialis anterior, EMG with Acc, EMG split across conditions, or none. Each model was additionally evaluated either by default with or without a temporal derivative (TD) of the ankle movement task regressor. Voxel-wise and post-hoc region-of-interest (ROI) analyses revealed that both Acc and EMG explained fMRI signal in the primary sensorimotor cortices, while EMG was additionally associated with activation in the cerebellar vermis and the secondary somatosensory cortex. The two latter findings were, however, neither reproduced when separating the signal fluctuations during rest and gait imagery nor reflected in pairwise comparisons. Leaving out the TD reduced each model's performance by increasing unexplained variance, but resulted in more signal being explained by the EMG or Acc in the cerebellum, reflecting that it preferentially exhibited brief signal changes during transitions between conditions. Taken together, both EMG and Acc enabled capturing specific brain activity related to the movement variability; however, including the TD may significantly affect the ability to detect EMG- or Acc-related signal in regions with transient fMRI responses sensitive to changes in movement context, such as the cerebellum.

title: Interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention: EEG evidence for joint modulation of late perceptual processing.
abstract: Voluntary action shapes our perception through sensory predictions of its consequences. These predictions are thought to inhibit perceptual processing of predicted outcomes, leading to sensory attenuation. However, some studies have reported findings that contrast with this effect, suggesting that the influence of predictions may reflect, or interact with, attentional processes. Here, we investigated the interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention on early and late perceptual processing, with prediction and attention referring to the likelihood of a sensory event and its behavioral relevance, respectively. Electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded while participants viewed two sequential gratings. The orientation of the first was either predicted and self-generated or unpredicted and externally generated. Participants judged the tilt direction of the second grating relative to the first but responded only when the grating appeared in a task-relevant color. EEG analyses revealed no modulation of early visual potentials (N1a), but modulations at later processing stages. Specifically, the P3b exhibited reduced amplitude for predicted compared to unpredicted stimuli, but only when they were task-relevant, whereas task-relevance enhanced the P3b only for unpredicted stimuli. Interestingly, multivariate pattern analysis showed significant temporal clusters for decoding the grating's orientation exclusively for predicted and task-relevant stimuli, although decoding performance did not significantly differ between conditions. Furthermore, predicted and task-relevant stimuli elicited faster behavioral responses, with prediction-related P3b latency differences correlating with reaction-time differences. Overall, converging findings from the P3b, multivariate, time-frequency and behavioral analyses provide suggestive evidence that top-down attention and action-based prediction may jointly facilitate late perceptual and decision-related processing.

title: Potential Mechanisms of N-Methyltyramine in Multitarget Regulation of Mental Disorders via the GPCR-cAMP Pathway.
abstract: N-Methyltyramine (NMT) is a tyramine derivative widely distributed in citrus plants and the traditional Chinese medicine Zhishi. Pharmacological studies have confirmed that NMT directly binds to the dopamine D₂ receptor (DRD2; Ki = 31.3µM), inhibits forskolin-induced cAMP accumulation (EC₅₀ ≈ 4µM, Emax = 89%), and dose-dependently antagonizes quinpirole-mediated β-arrestin2 recruitment, exhibiting G protein-biased agonistic properties. Meanwhile, NMT activates the human trace amine-associated receptor 1 (hTAAR1; EC₅₀ ≈ 2µM) to increase cAMP, possesses α₂-adrenergic receptor antagonistic activity (IC₅₀ = 5.53µM), and exhibits blood-brain barrier permeability (logPe = -5.16cm/s). Based on these multi-target receptor profiles, NMT may participate in the regulation of central monoaminergic neurotransmission via the GPCR-cAMP signaling axis, providing a new multi-target lead compound direction for research on neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, depression, and drug addiction. Notably, evidence for direct activation of β₂-adrenergic receptors by NMT remains insufficient, and its therapeutic effects and downstream signal integration mechanisms require NMT-specific experimental validation.

title: Cholinergic-Dependent Metaplasticity in the Amygdala-Insula Pathway During Incubation of Cocaine Craving.
abstract: The time-dependent increase in drug seeking during abstinence, termed 'incubation of craving' is believed to play a major role in the persistent risks of relapse. This phenomenon is associated with synaptic plasticity changes across brain structures involved in reward processing, executive functions, emotion regulation and inhibitory control. The basolateral amygdala (BLA) and the anterior insular cortex (aIC) are two interconnected structures involved in processing internal and external drug-related cues and are known to play a role in drug craving. However, whether chronic cocaine alters synaptic plasticity within the BLA-aIC circuit and how these changes evolve during abstinence remains unclear. Here, using cocaine self-administration and in vivo electrophysiological recordings in anesthetized male rats, we demonstrate that, while long-term potentiation in the BLA-aIC pathway remains intact, long-term depression is disrupted throughout abstinence in both cocaine- and sucrose-rats, indicating a persistent impairment in synaptic weakening mechanisms. Importantly, a loss of depotentiation was observed after late but not early abstinence, and was specific to cocaine self-administration, identifying it as a hallmark of incubation of craving. Systemic, but not local intra-aIC, blockade of muscarinic receptors with atropine restored depotentiation and reduced cocaine-seeking behavior. Finally, qPCR analysis revealed region-specific transcriptional adaptations, with upregulation of muscarinic, NMDA and AMPA receptor transcripts in the BLA and a selective decrease of Grin2a in the aIC. Together, these findings point to cholinergic regulation of BLA-aIC metaplasticity as a candidate mechanism underlying incubation of cocaine craving.

title: Therapeutic Potential and Toxicological Trade-Offs of Nanoparticle-Enhanced Valproic Acid in Glioblastoma: Behavioral and Oxidative Insights.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a poor prognosis. In the current research, the therapeutic and behavioral efficacy of valproic acid (VPA) and its nanoparticles (Nano VPA) with or without temozolomide (TMZ) was investigated in the C6 glioblastoma rat model. We divided eighty-four adult male Wistar rats into seven groups (n=12/group): sham, tumor, TMZ, VPA, nano VPA, VPA + TMZ, and nano VPA + TMZ. To induce tumors, C6 cells were injected into the brains of the rats. On days 12 to 15, behavioral performance was assessed using the social interaction test, elevated plus maze, open field, rotarod, and passive avoidance. On day 18, tumor size, edema, and histopathology were examined. Oxidative stress parameters in brain tissue and serum were measured by ELISA. VPA and Nano VPA significantly inhibited tumor growth, either alone or with TMZ. All treatments except Nano VPA + TMZ improved survival compared with tumor controls. Treated groups showed enhanced anxiety regulation, sociability, learning, and memory. Motor coordination improved following VPA or Nano VPA therapy. Tumor induction reduced serum SOD, CAT, and TAC levels; treatments raised serum TAC and lowered brain MDA, but further reduced serum SOD. Our results suggest that oxidative stress modulation may contribute to the neurobehavioral and antitumor effects of both VPA and nano-VPA. While nano-VPA showed greater tumor reduction, conventional VPA was more effective in improving survival. Combining VPA with TMZ may enhance outcomes, and support further study of Nano VPA as an adjuvant therapy for GBM.

title: Maternal piromelatine treatment is associated with attenuated behavioral alterations and sex-specific changes in hippocampal pCREB/BDNF signaling in adult offspring following prenatal constant-light exposure.
abstract: Maternal exposure to constant light during pregnancy (CLE) is associated with disrupted circadian organization and persistent behavioral alterations in adult offspring. This study examined behavioural performance and 24-hour locomotor activity patterns, as well as hippocampal pCREB and BDNF levels, in adult male and female offspring following prenatal CLE and maternal treatment with piromelatine (pir), which acts as an agonist at melatonin MT1/MT2 and serotonin 5-HT1A/5-HT1D receptors. Pregnant Wistar rats under light-dark regime received vehicle (veh), whereas dams exposed to CLE received vehicle (LL-veh), pir (10mg/kg), or melatonin. Compared to the LL-veh groups, offspring from pir-treated dams exhibited reduced anxiety- and depression-like responses and improved working memory in both sexes. Individual-subject cosinor analysis revealed heterogeneous 24-hour locomotor rhythmicity within and between groups. No significant treatment-group effect was detected for MESOR or amplitude, and the descriptive acrophase patterns did not provide evidence of treatment-induced restoration or normalization of circadian organization. Maternal pir treatment was associated with higher hippocampal pCREB and BDNF levels in male, but not female offspring relative to the LL-veh group. While the behavioral and molecular differences occurred concurrently in males, these findings do not prove that pCREB/BDNF signaling mediated the behavioral outcomes. Furthermore, the study cannot distinguish the direct developmental effects of maternal pir exposure from those mediated through maternal or offspring circadian rhythm. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as long-term behavioral and sex-specific molecular differences associated with maternal pir treatment rather than as evidence of circadian-independent antidepressant, anxiolytic, cognitive-enhancing, or BDNF-enhancing actions.

title: Brain folding as a Fourier series yields a developmental clock.
abstract: The human fetal cortex begins as a smooth spheroid and progressively folds into a stereotypical sulcal pattern. I show that the spherical-harmonic expansion - the closed-surface generalisation of Fourier's series - reproduces this developmental sequence in reverse on the group-average atlas: truncating the fully formed cortex at low maximum harmonic degree L_max recovers a younger fetal brain; progressively higher L_max recovers the primary, secondary and tertiary folds in the order in which they emerge. From this I derive a closed-form 23-dimensional log-fractional spectral descriptor. On atlas templates (17 Harvard CRL + 16 dHCP weekly templates) it predicts gestational age at MAE 0.13 and 0.38 wk across cohorts after a single supervised linear alignment, and 1.07 and 1.51 wk without. On 28 Yale-Wayne State longitudinal pairs it advances predicted GA in every subject, without cohort matching. On 80 FeTA scans (31 neurotypical, 49 pathological) off-trajectory distance discriminates pathology at AUC 0.80, and unsupervised clustering yields three internally stable, biometrically concordant subgroups - an exploratory finding requiring external validation. Individual-scan gestational-age accuracy is not the descriptor's competitive use (MAE 2.25 wk on FeTA-NT); its individual-scan value is the shape of the residual around the normative trajectory. The framework separates two spatial-scale regimes of folding onto distinguishable spectral bands and is complementary to existing measures of fetal cortical maturation.

title: Transdiagnostic Efficacy, Durability, and Optimal Parameters of rTMS for Cognitive Rehabilitation: A Comprehensive Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) is a promising non-invasive neuromodulation technique for cognitive rehabilitation. We evaluated the cognitive effects of rTMS on neurological and psychiatric diseases to determine moderators of efficacy. A meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs) comparing real versus sham rTMS to July 2025 was performed. Objective cognition reported as primary or secondary outcomes were extracted and Hedges' g effect sizes computed. Univariate and multivariate three-level meta-analyses were performed to estimate pooled effect sizes and assess moderator influence. 748 measures from 137 studies (5,972 participants) were extracted. Real rTMS produced a significant cognitive enhancement (g=0.28, p0.20, I2=35.8). Neurodegenerative (g=0.35) and focal (g=0.44) conditions demonstrated stronger effects than psychiatric conditions (g=0.20). Although stimulation target was not a significant moderator overall, the Inferior Frontal Gyrus showed the largest effect (g=0.45), with significant effects also at the left and right DLPFC and left parietal cortex (g=0.29-0.45), all nodes of the Frontoparietal Network. 1-Hz stimulation produced a significantly larger effect (g=0.39) than the 10-Hz reference (g=0.19); 5-Hz, 20-Hz and iTBS were also significantly positive (g=0.30-0.49). In multivariate models, adding 10 rTMS sessions improved cognitive outcomes (Δg=+0.077), whereas increasing the number of pulses per session trended toward reduced efficacy. All effects were confirmed in a left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex subgroup analysis. Subjective cognition was measured in only 6% of studies. A multivariate prediction tool is introduced: https://amsali.shinyapps.io/tms_cognition_prediction/ CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis demonstrates the sustained efficacy of rTMS in enhancing cognitive function, with small-to-moderate effect sizes across diverse clinical populations and stimulation protocols. However, a significant gap remains regarding whether these objective neurocognitive gains translate into meaningful improvements in subjective cognition or functional outcomes.

title: A Reproducible Safety Assessment Model for Concurrent Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation with Implanted Intracranial Electroencephalography Electrodes.
abstract: Concurrent transcranial magnetic stimulation and intracranial EEG (TMS-sEEG) offers a powerful approach for interrogating human brain circuits with high spatiotemporal resolution. However, standardized safety testing procedures for TMS in the presence of implanted electrodes are lacking. To establish and validate a reproducible methodological framework for assessing TMS safety with sEEG hardware, addressing potential risks of electrode displacement, heating, and secondary current induction. A conductive agarose phantom implanted with clinical-grade platinum sEEG electrodes was exposed to single-pulse TMS (0.4 Hz), repetitive TMS (1-50 Hz), and intermittent theta burst stimulation. Electrode displacement was quantified via high-speed video and motion tracking. Temperature changes were measured with fiber-optic thermal probes positioned at stimulated electrode contacts. Induced voltages were recorded using an oscilloscope and intracranial EEG hardware, and secondary current and charge density were calculated from oscilloscope outputs and impedance measurements. sEEG lead displacement remained micrometer-scale across stimulation conditions, with a maximum transient displacement of 10.99 μm and a maximum 1-s mean displacement from the pre-TMS position of 16.27 μm. Temperature changes remained well within the 2°C safety threshold across all tested conditions; in the primary temperature series, the maximum observed increase was 0.073°C. Induced voltages and charge densities remained below established safety limits, exhibiting consistent exponential decay with increasing distance from the coil. All stimulation conditions, including those exceeding typical clinical ranges, remained well within safety margins. Under the tested conditions in a controlled phantom environment, TMS exposure produced micrometer-scale transient and longer-timescale displacement, temperature changes within established safety thresholds, and charge densities within established safety thresholds. This validated methodological pipeline provides a standardized framework for future safety experiments involving TMS and implanted devices and supports continued development of TMS-sEEG as a tool for studying human brain circuitry and neuromodulation.

title: Investigating fatigability and cortical activation during prolonged foot tapping in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: People with multiple sclerosis (pwMS) often exhibit motor fatigability and reduced foot-tapping ability. However, the coupling between performance and cortical activity during fast, repetitive and prolonged ankle movements remains unexplored. We aimed to investigate the neural correlates of a prolonged foot-tap task (FTT) in pwMS and healthy controls (HC). Thirty-nine pwMS (EDSS 4[3.5], 55[14] years) and 18 HC (54.5[9.75) years) performed one 1-minute FTT for each foot. Wearable sensors and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) quantified motor performance and cortical activity, respectively. fNIRS covered bilaterally frontopolar, dorsolateral prefrontal, primary motor (M1) and supplementary motor area cortices. Data were segmented into 10-second intervals and analysed via two-way ANOVA (group × time). Spearman's correlations evaluated associations between changes in cortical activity and performance (6th vs 1st segment). PwMS showed worse FTT performance with lower DLPFC activation compared to HC. On the other hand, comparable FTT performance decline over time were observed in both pwMS and HC. Cortical activity increased in SMA in HC (6 vs 2-3 intervals), but not in pwMS. In HC's, increased cortical activity across all cortical regions in the 6th interval was positive and moderately associated with less worsening in tapping performance. On the other hand, increased M1 activity was weakly associated with less foot tapping in pwMS. PwMS exhibited reduced foot-tap performance, accompanied by reduced DLPFC activation. While increased cortical activity leads to better performance in HC (i.e., a neural compensatory strategy), in pwMS increased activity was associated with worse performance (i.e., neural inefficiency).

title: Cannabidiol's prosexual effects in sexually active and sexually inhibited male rats.
abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-intoxicating, psychoactive phytocannabinoid, is being explored for its therapeutic potential on a variety of disorders. Marketed as an over-the-counter drug, it is freely available to the public. As a central nervous system acting drug, CBD has the potential to produce sexual effects, especially after its chronic use. This study characterizes the sexual effects of acute and chronic CBD oral treatment in sexually experienced male rats that were either sexually active (n = 8 per group), as a model of optimal copulatory activity, or sexually satiated (n = 8 per group), as a model of inhibited sexual behavior and decreased sexual motivation. Acute administration of CBD to sexually active males produced biphasic, dose-dependent effects on mount and intromission latencies, parameters linked to sexual motivation. In sexually satiated rats, acute treatment with CBD reversed the sexual inhibitory state at a specific dose, which also increased sexual motivation in the sexual incentive motivation test. Chronic treatment (14 days) with low and high doses of CBD did not impair male rat sexual behavior expression in the sexually active male rats. Results show that acute ingestion of CBD has prosexual effects, mainly manifested in sexual motivation, which were particularly evident in the sexually inhibited male rats. CBD chronic treatment did not produce unwanted sexual effects in the sexually active males, suggesting that it does not negatively affect male sexual behavior. The therapeutic potential of acute treatment with CBD for sexual dysfunctions involving motivational deficits should be explored.

title: A natural neuronal receptor-derived MRI probe targets β-amyloid oligomers for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Early-to-mid detection of Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains challenging because clinically used amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) probes primarily visualize fibrillar β-amyloid (Aβ) deposits and require radioactive isotopes. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers a radiation-free alternative, but its application in molecular AD diagnosis is limited by insufficient blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and poor specificity toward early-to-mid Aβ species. Here, we developed a BBB-crossing liposomal MRI probe, Lipo@D1D2-Gd, by integrating a natural Aβ oligomer-binding receptor domain with a gadolinium chelator. The extracellular D1D2 domains of human leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor B2 (LilrB2), a neuronal receptor that recognizes neurotoxic Aβ oligomers, were recombinantly produced and bioorthogonally conjugated with a gadolinium chelator. The resulting D1D2-Gd retained its Aβ-binding capability and MRI contrast activity. To enable brain delivery, D1D2-Gd was encapsulated within maltose-functionalized PEGylated liposomes designed to facilitate BBB transport. After intravenous administration to 4-month-old 5xFAD mice, Lipo@D1D2-Gd crossed the BBB, accumulated in Aβ-rich brain regions, and generated MRI contrast enhancement that differentiated 5xFAD mice from wild-type controls. Systemic safety evaluation showed no obvious hematological, biochemical, or histological toxicity. This study establishes a receptor-derived, BBB-crossing biomaterial platform for radiation-free molecular imaging of early-to-mid AD-associated Aβ pathology. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: 1) Promising Targeting Strategy: We repurposed a human-derived natural receptor domain (LilrB2 D1D2) as a targeting module for β-amyloid (Aβ) oligomers, a key pathogenic species in Alzheimer's disease (AD). 2) Non-invasive MRI Approach: We constructed a liposomal probe designed to deliver the Gd-labeled targeting agent to the brain, enabling the detection of Aβ-associated pathology in 4-month-old 5xFAD mice via non-radioactive MRI, well before overt cognitive decline. 3) Experimental Validation: We demonstrate the probe's association with Aβ oligomers/plaques, effective BBB crossing, differences in MRI signals between AD model and wild-type mice, and an initially favorable biosafety profile, with no observed toxicity under the tested conditions. 4) Clinical Translation Potential: Our work presents a promising pathway toward a safe, accessible, and early-to-mid-stage AD screening tool, with the potential to facilitate population-wide screening and earlier therapeutic intervention.

title: Extraoral relocation of implant scanbody geometries: An in vitro comparison of two workflows for complete-arch implant position transfer.
abstract: To compare the metrological performance of an integrated extraoral GeoXact scanbody workflow (GXE; GeoXact® extraoral kit, Biotec srl, Vicenza, Italy) with a conventional intraoral implant scanbody workflow (ISB; Osstem TSIII, 4.8-mm platform; Osstem Implant Ltd., Busan, Republic of Korea) for complete-arch implant position transfer. A maxillary edentulous cast containing 6 digital laboratory analogs (TSMDLA, Osstem Implant Ltd., Busan, Republic of Korea) was scanned 15 times per workflow with one intraoral scanner (Primescan 2; Sirona Dental, Bensheim, Germany). Each experimental scan was compared with a workflow-specific structured-light reference after CAD-library replacement. The prespecified primary outcome was scan-averaged detrended translational magnitude; key secondary outcomes were global mean surface deviation and scan-averaged detrended angular deviation. Site-level and interimplant analyses were exploratory. GXE showed lower detrended translational magnitude (96 ± 52 µm vs 210 ± 72 µm; P < .001), global mean surface deviation (8 ± 3 µm vs 18 ± 16 µm; P = .041), and detrended angular deviation (0.121 ± 0.059° vs 0.320 ± 0.045°; P < .001) than conventional ISBs. Under the tested in vitro conditions, the integrated GXE workflow showed lower global surface deviation and smaller detrended translational and angular deviations than conventional ISBs. These metrological findings provide a basis for further prosthetic-fit and clinical validation. Under controlled in vitro conditions, the GXE workflow yielded lower global surface deviation and smaller relative translational and angular discrepancies than conventional ISBs.

title: Examining intersections of biographies & biologies: Diversity & outcomes of people with multiple sclerosis in Canada (iBio2Div-MS) protocol.
abstract: Although advances have been made in understanding multiple sclerosis (MS) disease etiology and developing new therapeutics, the benefits of these advances have been distributed inequitably across population groups. Persons with MS (PwMS) who are racialized, men, of lower social position, or living in rural areas experience worse outcomes for reasons yet to be fully elucidated. We designed a prospective three-year longitudinal study to assess the individual and joint effects of contextual, biographical, and biological factors (e.g., sex, age, and genetics), on performance-based and patient-reported outcomes among groups under-represented in MS research. We will enroll 500 PwMS and 100 individuals without MS who are aged ≥18 years, resident in Canada, able to complete interviews in English, commit to three years of participation, and self-identify as belonging to ≥1 of these groups: men, racialized, immigrant within the last ten years, 2SLGBTQI+, rural resident (population <10,000) or living with moderate-to-severe disability. Following e-consent, participants will provide a saliva sample for DNA collection and complete four telephone interviews over three years (at baseline and yearly thereafter). This study will provide insight into the joint contributions of contextual, biographical, and biological factors to health outcomes among underrepresented groups with MS.

title: Manifold view of spinal motor control: A paradigm in motion.
abstract: The neural manifold framework has transformed our understanding of cortical motor control, focusing on population dynamics that is constrained to low-dimensional structures in state space, where behaviors correspond to structured trajectories with characteristic topology. Yet the spinal cord, which houses the core circuitry responsible for rhythmic motor output such as walking, has remained largely unexplored from a manifold perspective. For decades, spinal motor function has been interpreted either through the lens of alternating flexor/extensor modules or through genetic characterization of interneurons. Both approaches struggle to amalgamate and explain how movement is flexibly generated, adapted, and stopped without losing posture. Here, we assess a new direction in spinal motor research with a focus on limbed locomotion, although we propose a general relevance, and argue that the neural manifold framework represents a complementary paradigm with the capacity to explain issues where the traditional view comes short.

title: Development of Italian centile curves for the North Star Ambulatory Assessment and timed items.
abstract: Centile curves may improve the interpretation of motor outcomes in specific populations. This study aimed to develop Italian age-specific centile curves for NSAA, rise-from-floor velocity (RFFV), and 10-meter walk/run velocity (10MWRV) in boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) and to assess their agreement with existing UK reference curves. Data from 627 patients (5080 assessments) with an age between 3-18 years were extracted from the Italian DMD Registry. GAMLSS models were used to estimate centile curves. Agreement with UK data (restricted to ages 5-16 years and who are actively on steroids) was evaluated using SDS deviation and percentile coverage analyses. NSAA scores peaked at approximately 6 years; RFFV and 10MWRV peaked at 5 years, then progressively declined. The Italian cohort showed small deviations from the UK centiles (all p<0.001): mean SDS values were significantly different across all outcomes, and age was significantly associated with SDS deviation through both linear and quadratic effects. The Italian centile curves extend reference data to wider age ranges. Available for both general and steroid-treated patients, they support clinical trials and real-world practice. The minor differences observed, especially in timed velocities, highlight the need for future international harmonisation.

title: Genomic, clinical, and radiological characterization of spontaneous cervical artery dissections: Findings from a single-center cohort.
abstract: The pathogenesis of spontaneous cervical artery dissection (sCeAD) remains incompletely understood. In this study, we performed a comprehensive clinical and radiological characterization of sCeAD patients and investigated rare variants in genes associated with vascular fragility using next-generation sequencing (NGS). From January 2021 to February 2025, we enrolled consecutive adult with sCeAD evaluated at the Neurology Department of our hospital. Patients presenting at least one feature suggestive of mendelian origin (positive family history, multi-territory vascular abnormalities, dysmorphological features) underwent genetic testing using an NGS panel including 62 genes related to vascular fragility. All patients underwent neurological, dysmorphological examinations and whole-body CT Angiography. Twenty-nine patients were enrolled (mean age 47.1 ± 10.7 years; 16 women, 55.2%). The internal carotid artery was the most frequently affected vessel by the index dissection (25/29, 86.2%). Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in two patients (COL1A1 and MYLK genes; 6.9%). Two patients (6.9%) were heterozygous for likely pathogenic variants associated with autosomal recessive conditions (COL4A3 and TNXB), while rare variants of uncertain significance were detected in 11 patients (37.9%).
